qualifier: For lawyers coming back after a career break, for family, health or any other reason, who wonder if the gap has closed the door.
symptom_title: The gap feels bigger than it is
symptom: You stepped away from law for a few years. Life needed you somewhere else, and you went. Now the children are in school, or things are settled, and the degree is still there.
But every time you think of going back, the same worry comes up. Who will hire someone whose CV has a blank space in the middle? Will the law have moved on without you?

You read about tech law and felt a spark. Then you wondered if a returning lawyer could really start in a new field, and you closed the page. This page is here to answer that doubt with the work itself.
outcome_title: What changes when the draft speaks first
outcome: Tech law is legal work for technology businesses: their contracts, policies, data privacy, compliance and disputes. A startup that needs its refund policy fixed asks one question: is this draft good? Nobody on that side asks when you last stood up in court.

You could return to law as a tech lawyer, working from home and building your own hours around family. The career is new, but the skill underneath it is the one you already trained for. You decide how fast it grows.
alternatives_title: Ways back that did not quite work

alternatives.t: Applying for the job you left
alternatives.why: Old-style hiring screens CVs first. The gap gets noticed before your ability does, and the conversation ends before it starts. You never get the chance to show what you can draft.

alternatives.t: Waiting until you feel fully ready
alternatives.why: Confidence usually comes from doing the work, not before it. Waiting for it first can quietly turn one year into three. The worry grows while the skill sits unused.
It updates what you know but leaves you with nothing to show. A client or firm still asks to see a document you have drafted, and a certificate alone cannot answer that.

reframe_title: Your draft is your CV now
reframe: In tech law, much of the work arrives as one task at a time: a refund policy, a set of terms, a contract. Each finished task becomes proof of what you can do, no matter when you last practised.

So the gap is a positioning problem, not a question of ability. You still know how to read carefully, ask the right question and put a promise into words. Those skills did not expire while you were away. The camp shows you where to point that skill.
cost_title: The quiet cost of putting it off
cost: Each month you spend unsure is a month the degree stays on the shelf. No one will push you to start, and that is the hard part. Three evenings from home is a gentle first step.
role_h2: What tech law work looks like for a lawyer back after a career break
role: You might start with an e-commerce store whose return policy is vague. You redraft it so the buyer knows when they can cancel, when they can return, how the return works, and how and when the refund arrives. It is a short document with real effects for the store and its buyers.

Next could be an influencer agreement for a brand. Five clauses carry most of it: the engagement and fee, the deliverables, the licence to use content, who owns the content, and the brand's guidelines. Each one is short enough to draft in a single sitting.

Over time you could review a startup's terms of use or help with privacy policies. Every piece is done on a laptop, in the hours you choose, and each one adds to a portfolio that speaks louder than the gap.
first_artifact: On Day 3 you draft an e-commerce cancellation, returns and refund policy in four parts, with the trainers, live. They walk through real examples from well-known online stores. You end the evening with a finished policy you can keep as your first work sample since the break.
longer_term: The plan from Day 2 asks for 2 hours a day: one hour of learning, one hour of outreach. It begins with the easiest skills, like policies and contracts. Over six months you could have several work samples, a few published articles, and a clear sense of the tech law work you enjoy most. If a week at home goes sideways, the plan simply picks up again the next day.

faq.q: My break was several years long. Is that too much?
faq.a: The camp's own priority list names lawyers returning after a break. The work is judged by the draft you send, and you begin with one document at a time. People see your work before they see your dates.

faq.q: Can I fit this around my children's routine?
faq.a: The camp is three evenings: Saturday and Sunday 6 to 9 PM IST, Monday 7 to 10 PM IST. The plan after it is about 2 hours a day, at times you choose.

faq.q: I have forgotten a lot of law. Will I keep up?
faq.a: Every skill is taught from the start, clause by clause. The refund policy, for example, is built in four simple parts with real examples shown on screen.

faq.q: What if I join and it is not right for me?
faq.a: The fee is Rs 10 including GST, and it is refundable. Sessions are live only with no recordings, so try to keep those evenings free.

closing_title: Lawyers back after a career break: start again with one draft
closing: Lawyers returning after a break can restart in tech law with a single document. In three live evenings you draft real policies and contracts with us, from home. The gap stays in the past, and your work becomes the first thing people see.
